hero.headline: Say yes to the automation work your clients keep asking for,
hero.subhead: A white-label build partnership that lets Harbor Lane sell AI automation under its own name, with NexusPoint doing the engineering behind the scenes.

diagnosis.label: The diagnosis
diagnosis.heading: The demand is real. The delivery capacity is not.
diagnosis.lead: Three of your retainer clients asked about AI automation this quarter, and each time the answer was a referral elsewhere.
diagnosis.lead_emphasis: That is revenue and relationship walking out of the door.
body: On our call you described the risk plainly: you cannot put your name on engineering work you cannot check, and a bad handover would cost you the client, not just the project.
So this proposal is built around delivery you can see. Every build runs in your tools, under your brand, with a weekly written update you can forward to the client unchanged.

pillars.label: Invisible
pillars.title: Your brand, your channels
pillars.body: We work inside your Slack and project board. The end client only ever hears from Harbor Lane.

pillars.label: Checkable
pillars.title: Evidence every week
pillars.body: A Friday update with what shipped, what is next and a short screen recording of the working system.

pillars.label: Owned
pillars.title: Clean handover
pillars.body: Documentation and video SOPs for every build, and IP assigned to you on delivery.

items.label: from signed scope to a working first workflow
live for your existing clients by the end of the pilot

targets.note: These are targets, not guarantees. They assume access to each client's tools within two working days of kickoff.

program.label: The 60-day pilot
program.heading: Start small. Prove it. Then scale.
program.intro: The pilot is sized so you can judge the partnership on real client work before committing to a standing arrangement.

phases.label: Scope
phases.title: Pick the first two builds
phases.body: We review the three client requests with you, choose the two with the clearest payoff and write a one-page scope for each.

phases.label: Build
phases.title: Ship under your name
phases.body: Both automations built, tested against real data and handed over inside your tools, with your team in the loop.

phases.label: Review
phases.title: Decide with evidence
phases.body: A joint review of time saved, client feedback and margin, then a recommendation on whether to continue.

rows.what: Kickoff, access to your tools, scope both builds with you and sign off the specs.
Build, test and hand over the first automation, then the second, with a Friday update each week.
Support both builds in production, fix anything that surfaces, run the pilot review.

included: Two automation builds scoped with you
Weekly written update and screen recording
Documentation and video SOPs for each build
30 days of fixes after each handover
not_included: Third-party software and AI model usage, billed at cost
Work for clients outside the agreed two builds
Direct contact with your end clients
from_you: A point of contact who can answer questions within a day
Access to each client's relevant tools
Sign-off on each scope before build starts

investment.heading: One partner behind your delivery.
investment.intro: Prices are wholesale, so you keep the margin when you resell. Software and model usage stay separate and visible.
investment.recommendation: We recommend the Pilot. It proves the partnership on two real client builds before you commit to capacity every month, and it credits in full toward the retainer if you continue within 30 days.

options.name: Single Build
options.summary: One scoped automation for one client, delivered under your brand.

options.name: Pilot
options.summary: Two builds over sixty days, with weekly updates and a joint review.

options.name: Overflow Retainer
options.summary: Standing build capacity for your clients, month to month.
includes: Up to three builds in progress

terms: Payment through Payoneer by card, US bank transfer (ACH) or wire. Invoices are in USD.
Mutual non-solicitation: we never contact your clients, and you do not hire our team directly, for 12 months.
IP for each build transfers to Harbor Lane on delivery.
Either side can end the retainer with 30 days notice after the initial term.
